title: gvrd championship grid 01
instruction:
You are Alba Reinholt, the tournament operations planner for Grindleford Valley Recreation District, and the state 12U championships are now your responsibility. Dunmarrow Logistics and Blackmarsh Fisheries are supporting the event, but the grid must work for the district's own six-field operation. The 44-team tournament runs from Friday 7 February through Sunday 9 February, and Carsten Alcantara needs a publishable match-and-referee grid by 3 February when the brackets close. Use the complete match, field, and referee information in `championship_source.xlsx`; it includes the bracket relationships, team paths, field characteristics, available time windows, and crew grades. Do not invent matches, teams, fields, or referees. Create `tournament_grid.xlsx` in the top level of the working directory you start in, using exactly that filename. This will be handed to Dmitri Sepulveda for publication and to Olamide Tikhonov for referee deployment, so it needs a clear day-by-day calendar/grid view and a supporting assignment or validation view that lets them check every match and crew without opening the source file. Numbered requirements: 1) place every listed match exactly once on one of the six named fields and one listed time slot, and assign exactly one available referee crew to it; 2) keep at least 90 minutes between any two appearances by the same team, including appearances connected through the bracket, and ensure a later-round match cannot begin before its prerequisite match has finished; 3) use only the two full-size fields for semifinals and the final, and observe the field-specific availability and maintenance closures in the source; 4) use the two lit fields only for the evening slots identified in the source, leaving every other field within its daylight window; 5) keep each grass field within its daily match limit and do not exceed the daily field and simultaneous-match capacities; 6) assign crews only when their listed grade qualifies them for that match, and do not put a crew on consecutive matches or overlapping matches; 7) respect the Sunday church-parking agreement by starting no Sunday match before 12:30, while still completing the final within the stated Sunday operating window; 8) make the calendar easy to scan by showing day, start and end time, field, stage, match identifier, teams or bracket positions, and referee crew in every scheduled entry; 9) include a concise validation view that identifies the counts of scheduled matches and crews, the daily and field totals, the lit/full-size usage, and any hard-rule exceptions, with zero exceptions in the completed plan. If a bracket position is not yet a named team, retain the source's bracket label rather than guessing a winner. Keep the workbook suitable for a broad public audience: use plain labels, consistent time notation, freeze or repeat useful headings, and make sure no entry is hidden behind truncation, filtering, or an overflow indicator. Do not add explanatory prose in place of a complete grid, do not change the source's match identifiers or crew names, and do not use internet data. Save only the requested workbook at the working-directory top level.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/championship_source.xlsx` — Authoritative tournament input containing the complete 44-team bracket and match relationships, six fields and their characteristics and closures, available slots, and referee crews with grades and availability.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `tournament_grid.xlsx` — A complete three-day tournament match and referee assignment grid with a public-facing calendar and supporting validation/assignment information. (Write at the top level of the starting working directory using exactly tournament_grid.xlsx.; Every source match must appear exactly once with one valid field, time slot, and referee crew.; All hard scheduling, field, bracket-rest, Sunday, capacity, and referee qualification rules must be satisfied.; Calendar entries must remain visible and readable without overflow or hidden rows.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

spec.professional_context: This is an operational scheduling deliverable for a first-time, multi-field youth championship. The workbook must be usable by a coordinator publishing the grid and a referee coordinator deploying crews.
difficulty_sources: Interlocking bracket precedence and 90-minute team-rest constraints across later rounds
Scarce lit and full-size field windows combined with a binding grass-field daily cap
Limited referee qualifications and a no-consecutive-match rule
Need to reconcile a solver-produced assignment with a readable public calendar and validation view

authoring_plan.source_file: Build championship_source.xlsx as the sole supplied reference. Include a fixed 44-team single-elimination bracket with 43 matches: preliminary, round-of-32, round-of-16, quarterfinal, semifinal, and final records. Use stable synthetic team names and bracket-position labels, with predecessor links for knockout matches. Include six named fields, exactly two full-size fields, exactly two lit fields, field operating windows, maintenance closures, the Sunday 12:30 start restriction, match duration and turnover information, and the grass-field daily cap. Include a finite pool of synthetic referee crews with availability dates, grade levels, and at least two scarce high-grade crews. Include a source slot calendar for Friday 7 February, Saturday 8 February, and Sunday 9 February. Do not use real identifiers or addresses.

constraints.assignment: Each of 43 matches is assigned exactly once to one source date-slot-field combination and one crew.
constraints.precedence: Every bracket predecessor ends before its dependent match starts; dependent matches also need the 90-minute team rest buffer where a lineage can continue.
constraints.rest: For any team or possible bracket lineage, appearances must be separated by at least 90 minutes from the earlier match end/start relation defined in the source.
constraints.fields: Semifinals and final use only full-size fields; closures and operating windows are hard exclusions; evening slots use only the two lit fields.
constraints.capacity: Each grass field has a daily cap of five matches; source simultaneous-match and field capacities must be respected. Make Friday/Saturday grass capacity and the scarce evening/full-size windows materially binding.
constraints.referees: Crew availability must contain the full match interval, grade must meet match requirement, overlapping assignments are forbidden, and consecutive source slots are forbidden. Make the highest grade qualification scarce for semifinals/final.
constraints.calendar: Sunday has no match before 12:30 and the final must finish within the source Sunday close.

authoring_plan.tightness: Target approximately 0.72 feasible-set tightness. Ensure a naive earliest-slot greedy assignment encounters a blocked field, rest, or scarce-grade decision and needs backtracking or deliberate balancing, while retaining multiple feasible schedules.
authoring_plan.gold: Run an offline constraint solver over the generated source instance, retain one feasible schedule, and emit the checker from the predicates above rather than hard-coded cell answers. Independently verify all 43 IDs, precedence paths, 90-minute rest relations, field closures, grass caps, lit/full-size restrictions, Sunday window, crew availability/qualification, non-overlap, and no-consecutive-slot rules. Render and inspect the workbook; confirm every calendar entry is visible and the validation totals reconcile. The reference solution passed all rubric items.
